title: Refine implicit-surface weights with chain-aware influence domains
description:
## Explicit anatomy requirement

The weighting system must remain general-purpose: it must not assume biped or quadruped topology. Any number of limbs, in any authored order and at any valid Body position, must be supported without limb-count modes or species-specific branches.

## Summary
Refine the MVP welded-surface weighting model with explicit anatomical influence domains and prove that posed body/limb motion does not create visibly incorrect cross-body smearing.

## Current state
The domain-aware refinement is implemented. `InfluenceDomain[]` is supplied by the live runtime preview to `CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer.Bind`; Body radius preparation uses the compact anatomical Body rig; and the topology dependency is resolved. `ImplicitSurfaceInfluenceDomainResolver` now resolves a primary geometry domain plus its intended non-Body authored ancestors. Child geometry therefore may blend with its owning limb chain while sibling and opposite-side chains remain ineligible.

## Newly observed risk
User visual validation on `dinus_uprightus` shows general mesh smearing/weird deformation when Body rig parts are moved. Do not assume this is caused by chain-domain attribution alone. Characterize actual generated `BoneWeight` distributions and a controlled one-bone pose before changing the falloff radius or introducing another heuristic. The current closest-point-on-segment weighting model must be preserved unless measured evidence identifies it as the source.

## Acceptance
Preserve TSK-0131 closest-segment distance, morphology radii, deterministic top-four selection, normalization, mirror behavior, and build-time ownership. Prove hip, shoulder, mirrored, branch, knee, elbow, child-geometry, and controlled Body-segment deformation locality. A one-bone pose must not produce long-range smearing into unrelated Body regions beyond the documented blend neighborhood. The domain contract must remain independent of limb count, authored order, and attachment position.

## Remaining gate
Executable Unity generated-geometry validation is still required. The task must not be marked Done based solely on source/build inspection. Foot-grounding remains separate.

## Evidence
Focused resolver regression coverage proves child-domain inclusion, sibling exclusion, and mirrored parent-chain isolation. Generated-creature visual validation is now also required for deformation locality. See the skeleton/animation audit documents under `docs/audits/` on `audit/skeleton-animation-improvements-2026-09-07`.

## Performance note
Domain hierarchy construction is now cached once per resolved part/side during binding preparation instead of allocating a `List<string>`/array for every welded vertex. This is a build-time optimization only; it does not alter influence eligibility or the per-frame animation path.

comments.body: Topology blocker resolved by TSK-0148 implementation. The runtime seam is connected: live preview supplies InfluenceDomain[] into CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer.Bind. Keep InProgress pending executable generated-geometry validation; do not merge the separate foot-grounding issue into this task.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Hierarchy-domain hardening: welded-surface geometry now resolves its own part domain plus non-Body authored ancestor domains. This allows foot/hand child geometry to blend with its owning limb chain while excluding sibling and opposite-side chains. Added focused runtime resolver coverage for owned-parent inclusion, sibling exclusion, and mirrored-parent isolation. Unity/generated-creature validation remains the closure gate.

comments.body: User visual validation (2026-09-07): moving Body rig parts causes noticeable mesh smearing/weird deformation on `dinus_uprightus`. This is not yet assigned to a specific algorithmic cause. Next validation must inspect actual `BoneWeight` distributions and a controlled one-bone pose before changing falloff/weight policy. Preserve performance by keeping any repair build-time only.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Build-time performance hardening: `ImplicitSurfaceInfluenceDomainResolver` now constructs immutable hierarchy domains once per resolved part and mirror side, then reuses those structs across all vertices. The previous implementation allocated the hierarchy `List`/string array for every vertex. Domain eligibility and the per-frame animation path are unchanged.

## Audit synthesis disposition (2026-09-10)
F-13's finite-radius builder inconsistency is fixed at the source boundary in the current branch, but Unity/generated-creature closure remains open. Keep this task InProgress and do not create a duplicate radius task. Continue with controlled generated-body deformation evidence.

comments.author: ChatGPT
comments.body: Static reproduction diagnosis: ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring.Author previously threw when an explicit InfluenceDomain excluded every positive falloff candidate. The runtime binding path always supplies generated InfluenceDomain[] and therefore could abort regeneration on valid welded vertices that fell just outside the finite weighting tube. Fixed in commit 841e85ce479d0315d6f68a000d5d4d994d785a69: when a domain-constrained vertex has no positive falloff candidate, choose the nearest segment admitted by that already-resolved domain, deterministically tie-breaking by BoneIndex, with weight 1.0. No sibling/opposite-side fallback is permitted. The unrestricted helper remains strict. Unity/generated-creature deformation validation remains required.
